title.narrative: Economic Recovery for Conflict Affected People - ERCAP
Economic Recovery for Conflict Affected People - ERCAP

description.narrative:
Overall goal
Enhanced economic adaptation, protection and recovery of conflict-affected populationsand other vulnerable community members, through an inclusive, innovative, gender- and conflict-sensitive, and climate-smart systems development approach.
Objectives/Outcomes
Through inclusive, market-based solutions, the programme is expected to influence systems change to enable the following:
Outcome 1: Conflict-affected communities have resilient livelihoods through improved productivity and production of targeted crops and livestock value chains, climate-smart systems and access to income-generating opportunities (self and wage work) through strengthening Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) through appropriate Business Development Services.
Outcome 2: Conflict-affected communities and MSMEs use a range of appropriate and affordable financial products, climate smart technologies, instruments to create and enhance livelihood opportunities through strengthened financial service providers' capacities as well as support to the target communities to have the required financial literacy and capability to utilise financial services.
Outcome 3: Vulnerable conflict-affected communities have improved capacity to mitigate and reduce protection risks through access to justice, community support mechanisms, and psychosocial support, including access to early recovery support protection capacity enhancement support across the displacement cycle.
The core of this proposed project is aimed at improving the economic adaptation, protection, and recovery of populations affected by conflict.
Övergripande syfte i det föreslagna projektet är att bidra till förbättrad ekonomisk återhämtning, reducera sårbarhet och bidra till återhämtning för människor som drabbats av konflikter.

sector.narrative: Education/training in banking and financial services

description.narrative:
As this is the first year of implementation and mainly covering the inception period, early results have focused on reach.
Major achievements during the reporting period includes:
Signs of systemic change: Primarily observed in financial insititution adaptation, market buy-in in goat value chain and promising horticulture engagement. For example, financial institutions have modified loan provisions and targeted underserved groups, including women and IDPS, going beyond their initial agreements. The goat value chain intervention shows promising behavioural shifts with agro-vets.
Reach: During the early stage of implementation ER-CAP has achieved 99.3% of household target for the reporting period. Initial reach is at 13.3% of overall programme goal in the early implementation phase (3-6 months). The reach for host communities exceed the target (130%) and returnee was at 89% reach. IDP reach was at 30% of the target.
Trainings: 780 participants, of which 528 women, received training to enhance financial literacy, agricultural practicies and resilience in conflict-affected areas. Mercy Corps focused on practical skills, First Consult on financial education and Danish Refugee Council on VSLA development.
Mercy Corps: 81.1% of participant target reached, 19% of 5-year reach/plan achieved
Danish Refugee Council: Household reach of 93.4%. Established 18 VSLAs (25 members each, a total of 450 participants) which exceeds the target. 1.4M ETB saved, 575k ETB loans disbursed to 62 members from their own savings.
First Consult: 140% of 2024 target achieved, 30M ETB loan disbursed and thus far exceeding the goal of 7.5 million, average 30k per enterprise .
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
